skill.name: perigon-agent
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents to follow Perigon project conventions, file locations, and implementation defaults.
skill.summary: Apply Perigon coding conventions before generating project code.
skill.author: AterDev

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from instructional prose in SKILL.md. The hardcoded URL is a documentation reference, and the flagged reconnaissance lines describe project conventions and caution against automatic builds or migrations.

static_findings.snippet: - Key docs: Development-Conventions, Manager-Business-Logic, Controller-APIs, Database, Data-Access,
- Behavior defaults: RESTful APIs; ManagerBase pattern; Code First EF; Guid v7 IDs; BusinessExceptio

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 contains a public documentation URL for Perigon conventions. It does not instruct the agent to make network requests or transmit data.
Line 13 lists preferred implementation patterns such as REST APIs and Entity Framework defaults. It does not request host inspection, credential discovery, or system reconnaissance.
Line 14 tells the agent to ask for clarification and avoid auto-running builds or migrations. This reduces operational risk rather than enabling reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Perigon projects need agents to follow established backend, frontend, and documentation rules. This skill points Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward the right conventions before code generation.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to the global Copilot instructions before code work.
Maps backend entity, manager, DTO, controller, and host locations.
Maps Angular routes, services, shared components, and i18n paths.
References Perigon documentation for development, database, controller, and data-access conventions.
States default API, manager, ID, exception, projection, and response-wrapper practices.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not generate code by itself.
It depends on separate Perigon documentation for complete rules.
It does not validate generated code or run project diagnostics.
It avoids automatic builds and migrations unless the user asks.

use_cases.title: Add a Backend Feature
use_cases.description: Use the skill to find the expected service, manager, DTO, and controller locations before creating a feature.

use_cases.title: Update Angular Client Code
use_cases.description: Use the skill to place route, service, shared component, and translation changes in the expected frontend folders.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Output
use_cases.description: Use the skill to check whether generated work follows Perigon defaults for APIs, exceptions, managers, and database access.

prompt_templates.title: Find Project Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a task with the correct Perigon context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the perigon-agent skill. Identify the relevant Perigon instructions and project locations for my requested change before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the perigon-agent skill to plan a Perigon feature. List the backend and frontend files likely involved, then wait for my confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Implement With Defaults
prompt_templates.scenario: Create code that follows established conventions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the perigon-agent skill while implementing this change. Follow RESTful API, ManagerBase, Code First, Guid v7, and BusinessException conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Generated Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the perigon-agent skill to review this change. Check folder placement, API shape, manager calls, database access, projections, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a new customer endpoint for a Perigon service.
output_examples.output: The agent identifies the controller, manager, DTO, and entity folders, then recommends a RESTful endpoint using the existing manager pattern.
The agent checks for Code First usage, Guid v7 identifiers, efficient projections, and avoided heavy Include calls.

output_examples.input: Update an Angular route and translation.
output_examples.output: The agent points to the route file, service folder, shared component area, and i18n asset path before editing.

best_practices: Start with the global Copilot instructions before changing code.
Ask for missing entity, DTO, module, or service details before implementation.
Use the linked Perigon docs when local guidance is not enough.
anti_patterns: Do not invent folder locations when the skill lists the expected map.
Do not auto-run builds or migrations unless the user requests them.
Do not wrap API responses when the conventions reject ApiResponse wrappers.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides AI coding agents to follow Perigon project structure, documentation, and implementation defaults.

faq.question: Does it generate code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It supplies context and rules that an agent should apply during coding tasks.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No direct network action is required. It includes a public documentation URL for optional reference.

faq.question: Can it run builds or migrations?
faq.answer: The skill advises agents to avoid auto-running builds or migrations unless the user asks.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before Perigon code generation, feature planning, or review of generated implementation changes.
